tutor.en: Yes? Are you looking for something?

options.why: 'Kde je' asks where something is; 'kam' asks where TO (a direction).
The subject stands in the nominative: 'hlavná stanica', not 'stanici'.

tutor.sk: Hlavná stanica? Idete pešo alebo vlakom?
tutor.en: The main station? Are you going on foot or by train?

options.sk: Idú pešo, prosím. Je to ďaleko?
options.why: 'Idú' is they go; one person going now says 'idem'.

options.sk: Chodím pešo, prosím. Je to ďaleko?
options.why: For this one journey you go 'idem' (ísť); 'chodím' means I go there regularly (chodiť).

tutor.sk: Nie je to ďaleko. Desať minút priamo po Obchodnej.
tutor.en: It is not far. Ten minutes straight along Obchodná.

options.why: 'Po' meaning along takes the locative: 'po Obchodnej'; 'Obchodnou' is instrumental.
Along the street is 'po Obchodnej'; 'do' would mean into the street.
'Mám' takes the accusative object: 'mám mapu', not 'mapa'.
'Mapu' is the accusative object; 'mape' is the locative.

tutor.sk: Dobre. Potom vľavo na Hlavné námestie. Stanica je naproti.
tutor.en: Good. Then left onto Hlavné námestie. The station is opposite.

options.why: Direction takes the accusative: 'na Hlavné námestie'; 'námestiu' is a locative form.
The adjective must agree with the neuter noun: 'Hlavné námestie', not 'Hlavní'.

tutor.sk: Presne tak. Desať minút, nie viac.
tutor.en: Exactly so. Ten minutes, no more.

options.why: 'Kde bude' asks where it will be; 'kam' asks for a direction.

tutor.en: It is, by the exit. Have a good journey!

options.why: When you leave you say 'dovidenia'; 'dobrý deň' is the greeting.
Goodbye is written as one word: 'dovidenia'.
